title: Weak predictable SESSIONID with insecure meta cookie delivery
snippet: content += "Welcome %s" % (re.sub(r"[^\w]", "", params.get("username", "")), "".join(random.sample(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 20)))
evidence: content += "Welcome %s" % (re.sub(r"[^\w]", "", params.get("username", "")), "".join(random.sample(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 20))) | validator: dsvw.py:67-68 SESSIONID from random.sample never stored/checked anywhere; no session enforcement so predictability crosses no boundary, meta Set-Cookie decorative | refute: not_a_vulnerability | consensus: 1/1 fp | triage: SESSIONID never stored or checked; decorative meta tag FP
rationale: WHO: remote client receives SESSIONID after login. HOW: token built with random.sample (Mersenne Twister, non-CSPRNG) and delivered via meta http-equiv Set-Cookie without Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite and without server-side binding. WHAT: breaks unpredictability and cookie-confinement invariants enabling prediction and fixation.
conditions: Unauthenticated remote GET to /login with valid credentials; attacker can observe/sample SESSIONID
hunter_evidence: content += "Welcome %s" % (re.sub(r"[^\w]", "", params.get("username", "")), "".join(random.sample(string.ascii_letters + string.digits, 20)))

rationale: WHO: server operator sends response headers to victim browsers. HOW: handler explicitly sends X-XSS-Protection: 0 on every response disabling built-in reflected-XSS filtering. WHAT: breaks defense-in-depth invariant removing client-side mitigation for the reflected vectors.

title: Concurrent race on shared SQLite connection

refs.note: global sqlite connection shared across threads

evidence: connection = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False) | validator: dsvw.py:17 shared :memory: connection with ThreadingServer dsvw.py:84-86 causes only robustness errors; no auth/access boundary crossed | refute: not_a_vulnerability | consensus: 1/1 fp | triage: Shared memory connection causes robustness errors only, no boundary FP
rationale: WHO: concurrent remote clients share global connection via ThreadingMixIn. HOW: init creates single sqlite3 connection with check_same_thread=False and each do_GET uses connection.cursor() without locking. WHAT: breaks thread-confinement invariant enabling cursor-state races and database corruption.
conditions: Concurrent unauthenticated requests to threaded server
hunter_evidence: connection = sqlite3.connect(":memory:", isolation_level=None, check_same_thread=False)

triage.rationale: Robustness race only: no access boundary crossed
